title: Your sandugo ally asks for help
story: A messenger from {neighbor} arrives soaked from the river. A storm has torn the roofs from their houses, and {datu} asks for timber, as one bound to you by blood.

choices.label: Send timber
choices.result: Your canoes carry beams and bamboo upriver. {datu} sends back word of deep thanks.

choices.label: Send what can be spared
choices.result: A few bundles of bamboo go upriver. It is not much, and {datu} knows it.

choices.label: We have nothing to spare
choices.result: The messenger leaves without a word. A blood compact is not easily forgotten, nor is a refusal.

_note: A sandugo (blood compact) bound two leaders and their people to help one another.
sources: Antonio Pigafetta, Report on the First Voyage Around the World (1525), on the blood compact at Limasawa and Cebu
William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
